name: RECOIL-v2
mechanism: Lab-UUID marker cascade: every OS artifact (scheduled task, Run-key, exec beacon, exfil file) carries the engagement lab-UUID, and the wipe walks the FULL cascade — each artifact's removal unblocks the next in dependency order — then runs a SHA-256 zero-survivor audit over every node, proving no marker survives anywhere.
what_it_does_previous_couldnt: Wipe removed artifacts greedily; if one removal depended on another having succeeded, order could leave a straggler. The marker cascade makes removal order-aware and dependency-complete, and the SHA-audit enumerates EVERY node so zero-survivor is exhaustive, not sampled.
fireback: The operator sees the wipe report list every cascade node with its SHA-256 and the final zero-survivor verdict — the full set of what was planted and what is now gone. Fireback = perfect forensic honesty: nothing the tool made is left to be found later.
containment: The cascade touches only engagement-marker artifacts on the operator's host (prefix/hive scoped); every removal target is asserted to carry the marker before deletion; the audit covers only marker-carrying paths; nothing outside scope is ever touched.
kill_switch: The kill-switch IS this cascade wipe: it removes each node in dependency order, re-queries/re-reads to prove absence, and emits the exhaustive zero-survivor audit. A --cascade-dry flag previews the removal order before any byte is touched.
novelty_angle: Cleanup is elevated to an order-aware, dependency-complete, exhaustively-audited graph walk over the engagement's own marker cascade — reversible persistence by construction where removing everything is as rigorous as planting it.
